standard.title: Recognise rhyme, alliteration and phonemes
standard.description: recognise and generate rhyming words, alliteration patterns, syllables and sounds (phonemes) in spoken words (phonological awareness)
standard.prior_knowledge: Students may have heard rhymes and songs. They have not yet been asked to consciously attend to, name and generate the phonological patterns in spoken words — rhyme, alliteration, syllables and phonemes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can recognise and generate rhyming words, identify alliteration patterns, identify syllables in spoken words, and isolate phonemes — demonstrating phonological awareness across multiple word types.

nodes.label: Rhyming words share endings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a rhyming pair and produce a rhyming word when given a target.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify whether two words rhyme; generate one word that rhymes with a given word.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and produce rhyming words; identify rhyming patterns in familiar stories and rhymes; generate rhyming strings.
wider: Generate rhyming strings across multiple word families — exploring how many words share the same rime
Compare rhyming conventions in English with other languages or First Nations Australian language patterns known to students
Create simple rhyming couplets orally — applying rhyme generation to creative language play
nodes.hinge_reason: Reliable rhyme recognition signals that phoneme-level auditory discrimination is developing — without this, phoneme isolation in Node 4 and the blending and segmenting tasks in LY10 will be unreliable, as they all depend on the ability to hear and attend to sounds within words.

response_modes.reason: Reliable rhyme recognition and production is foundational to phonological awareness — errors here indicate the phoneme-level awareness needed for decoding is not yet secure. Practice across many word pairs is the remedy.

success_criteria: Student can identify whether two words rhyme when heard.
Student can generate at least one rhyming word when given a target word.

nodes.label: Alliteration is repeated initial sounds
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify alliteration patterns in spoken words — recognising that initial sounds repeat.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify an alliteration pattern in two words (e.g. 'helpful Henry').
nodes.typical_width: Identify alliteration patterns in spoken words and familiar texts; produce simple alliterative phrases; understand that alliteration is about the initial sound, not the initial letter.
wider: Create alliterative name phrases for each class member — exploring alliteration productively
Identify alliteration in poems, picture book titles and tongue twisters across a range of texts
Compare alliteration in English with sound-play patterns in other languages
success_criteria: Student can identify two words that start with the same sound.
Student can produce at least one alliterative phrase orally.

nodes.label: Words have syllables
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the number of syllables in spoken words by clapping, tapping or counting.
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly identify the number of syllables in at least five words of varying length (one to three syllables).
nodes.typical_width: Identify syllables in spoken words by clapping or tapping; segment multi-syllable words; understand that every syllable contains a vowel sound.
wider: Clap syllables across names of class members, local area names and topic words — exploring syllable patterns in real vocabulary
Compare syllable counts in familiar words across different languages — noting that syllable structure differs across languages
Sort word cards by syllable count — building a syllable-based word awareness
success_criteria: Student can clap the correct number of syllables in a spoken word.
Student correctly distinguishes one-syllable and two-syllable words.

nodes.label: Words are made of phonemes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can isolate individual phonemes in spoken words — hearing the discrete sounds that make up a word.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the first phoneme in at least three spoken words.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise individual phonemes in spoken words; isolate initial, medial and final phonemes; understand that words are made of discrete sounds.
wider: Practise phoneme isolation across a range of word types — varying initial, medial and final positions
Compare phonemes in English words with sounds in other languages or names familiar to students — noticing sounds that English does and doesn't have
Use phoneme awareness as a bridge to letter-sound knowledge — connecting isolated phonemes to their grapheme representations
nodes.hinge_reason: Phoneme isolation is a prerequisite for blending and segmenting in LY10 — students cannot blend phonemes they cannot yet isolate, and cannot segment words into phonemes they cannot hear as discrete units.

response_modes.reason: Phoneme isolation is a prerequisite for blending and segmenting (AC9EFLY10) — without reliable phoneme isolation, decoding will be unreliable. Practice to accuracy is required before width is productive.

success_criteria: Student can isolate the first phoneme in a spoken word.
Student can isolate the final phoneme in a spoken CVC word.
Student understands that words are made of more than one sound.
